event_text: USS Constellation (1854), the last all-sail warship built by the United States Navy and current museum ship in Baltimore Harbor, is commissioned.
headline: USS Constellation Sets Sail as Last All-Sail Warship
story: Barry and Susan perched on a rusty anchor, watching the USS Constellation cut through the Baltimore Harbor waters. 'Ah, 1854, and the Yanks are launching their last all-sail warship,' Barry said, eyeing the vessel's majestic sails. 'The Constellation, a 22-gun sloop, designed to outrun and outgun any opponent, or so the theory goes.' Susan cocked her head. 'Rather like commissioning a cavalry unit just as the first tanks are rolling off the production line, isn't it? The writing's on the wall for sail, Barry.' Barry sniffed. 'Still, she's a beauty. And the Americans are nothing if not sentimental – they'll squeeze every last bit of use out of her, even as the age of steam is dawning.' Susan ruffled her feathers. 'And what a dawn it is – the Crimean War's just kicked off, and the Constellation will likely see action soon enough. Though I suppose it's comforting to know she'll eventually become a museum ship, a relic of a bygone era, moored safely in this very harbor.'
regret_line: A mere trifle, really, considering they were just delaying the inevitable march of progress.
winner_line: The shipbuilders, who managed to squeeze in one final, glorious all-sail commission before the age of steam took over.
